title: Fall back to a backup, and keep both failures when it fails too

blocks.text: Code inside a `catch` block can throw too, and when it does, the exception that was being handled is lost unless you keep it.
Write `FallbackReader.read(Source primary, Source backup, String name)`:

items: when that throws an `IOException`, it returns `backup.read(name)` instead;
when the backup throws an `IOException` as well, `read` throws **the backup's** exception, with the primary's exception added to it through `addSuppressed`.

blocks.text: A backup is for I/O failures only; a bug in the primary is not something to paper over.

cases.says: It reads from the primary and leaves the backup alone when the primary works.
When the primary throws an IOException it reads from the backup.
When the backup read in the catch block throws too, that failure is thrown with the primary's attached as suppressed.
Only an IOException sends the read to the backup; an unchecked failure of the primary reaches the caller.
When both fail, the backup's exception is the one thrown, with the primary's inside it, not the other way round.

concepts: Code in a catch block can throw too, and the exception being handled is lost unless it is kept.
